entry.title: Morning Digest, August 26, 2026
entry.content:
Trujillo Times

Wednesday, August 26, 2026 — Mostly sunny with a chance of showers and thunderstorms after 2pm, high near 91°F; overnight low around 70°F.

At a Glance

  • Mostly sunny today with a chance of showers and thunderstorms after 2pm, high near 91°F (heat index up to 97); overnight low around 70°F.
  • Fantasy Football Draft tonight at 6:00 PM; next up is Kate & Jack's Engagement Party on Saturday evening.
  • Portfolio section unavailable — no holdings configured in DigestConfig.md.
  • U.S. futures were flat to lower ahead of Nvidia's earnings and the Fed's inflation gauge; Alibaba shares sank 10% on a $10.2 billion AI-infrastructure share sale.
  • No games today for Barcelona, the Vikings, or Miami; Barcelona hosts Athletic Club Thursday, and Gavi's knee knock from the Elche win was only a bruise.
  • The Verge led newsletters with five new items, including Garmin's new Fenix 9 watches and a free Witcher 3 remaster coming September 29.

Calendar

Today

  • Fantasy Football Draft — 6:00 PM

Coming up: Sat Aug 29, 6:00 PM — Kate & Jack's Engagement Party.

Newsletters

The Art of Manliness — One new piece: Marine veteran Mike LeBlanc, author of What If Anger Is the Answer?, makes the case for cultivating thumos — the ancient Greek mix of spiritedness, pride, and honor-driven ambition — as a source of self-discipline and effective leadership rather than something to suppress.

The Verge — Five new items: Garmin launched its Fenix 9 and Fenix 9 Pro rugged smartwatches (from $999.99), with brighter OLED screens, a faster map engine, and a titanium/solar Pro model rated for up to 57 days of battery life. The Trump administration is raising the H-1B visa fee to $103,265 after a court struck down its earlier $100,000 fee, and separately plans to revoke up to 200,000 asylum seekers' visas in what would be the largest mass visa revocation in U.S. history. Humble is selling Daniel Mullins' deckbuilder Inscryption for $7.99 ahead of his upcoming Pony Island 2. CD Projekt Red will release a free remaster of The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt on September 29th with improved visuals, combat, and a reworked skill tree, part of a push that includes a 2027 expansion and The Witcher 4 in 2028. And Chinese vacuum maker Dreame shut down its car division after government funding dried up, with former employees saying its flashy rocket-boosted concept car was never a real, drivable vehicle.

Cool Material — One new piece, "The Luxury Lover's Guide to Puerto Vallarta," but the source page was unavailable behind a bot-detection block, so no summary could be produced.

Uncrate — Five new items: BMW built just ten commemorative R 1300 GS Adventure motorcycles marking 10 years of production at its Manaus, Brazil plant, each with an olive-drab finish and an Akrapovič exhaust. A limited, numbered print of Terry O'Neill's 1975 photo of Robert Redford on his motorcycle is priced at $189 but already sold out. A Levi's-presented lookbook built a faded, monochromatic look around a $60 crewneck, a $35 pocket tee, and $85 carpenter jeans. A $48 hand-blown crystal glass designed over two years to enhance the aroma of mezcal and tequila is down to its last unit. And The Luminaire is offering a customizable six-day helicopter-and-train tour of Mexico's agave regions, including distillery visits and a rooftop mezcal mixology class.

News

Stock market

  • Bloomberg — U.S. futures were flat to lower (S&P 500 -0.1%, Nasdaq 100 -0.2%) as traders stayed cautious ahead of Nvidia's earnings report, seen as a bellwether for the AI trade, and the Fed's preferred inflation gauge due later this week.

Geopolitics

  • The Cipher Brief / FDD — Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent unveiled "Operation Economic Outcast," a new sanctions push expanding into aviation, digital assets, gold, and shipping while designating nearly 60 entities tied to Iran's nuclear and missile programs.

Technology

  • Reuters — Alibaba shares plunged about 10% after the company announced a $10.2 billion share placement to fund a major AI-infrastructure push, spooking investors over near-term dilution.

AI

  • Tech Startups / AI Herald — OpenAI began previewing an "Ultrafast" mode for its GPT-5.6 Sol model that runs up to 14x faster than the standard version, alongside a temporary 20%-plus API price cut, as the frontier price-and-speed race with Anthropic and Google continues.

Tech business, startups, and VC

  • AlleyWatch — Coffee and matcha chain Blank Street raised a $75 million Series C led by General Atlantic, with General Catalyst, Left Lane Capital, and Tiger Global also participating.

Golf equipment

Nothing notable today.

Pokémon investing

Nothing notable today.

Sports

No games today for Barcelona, the Vikings, or Miami; Barcelona hosts Athletic Club at Camp Nou on Thursday, and Gavi's knee knock from the Elche win was only a bruise.

F.C. Barcelona

  • Barca Blaugranes — Gavi picked up a knee knock in Barcelona's 5-0 rout of Elche in the LaLiga opener, but scans showed only a bruise and he's expected to be fit; Frenkie de Jong and Roony Bardghji remain unavailable.
  • Goal.com / Sports Mole — Barcelona host Athletic Club at Camp Nou on Thursday, August 27 in their home league opener, riding a five-match unbeaten head-to-head streak against the Basque side.

Minnesota Vikings

  • Star Tribune — Backup quarterback J.J. McCarthy and Carson Wentz split second-team reps at Tuesday's practice as the team nears Saturday's roster cutdown, with McCarthy still banged up from the preseason loss to Baltimore.
  • ESPN — The Vikings front office has already fielded trade calls on McCarthy, whose grip on the No. 2 quarterback job behind Kyler Murray looks shaky heading into final cuts.

Miami Hurricanes

  • Miami Hurricanes / SI — Quarterback Darian Mensah was voted preseason ACC Player of the Year and, along with receiver Malachi Toney and running back Mark Fletcher Jr., landed on the Maxwell Award watch list as camp wraps up; the Hurricanes open the season at Stanford on September 4, followed by a home opener against Florida A&M on September 10.

Soccer transfer rumors

  • ESPN / Football365 — With deadline day approaching (the "Big 5" European windows close August 31–September 1), Liverpool are reportedly closing in on Bradley Barcola from PSG and also pursuing Brighton's Yankuba Minteh, while AC Milan have agreed a deal with Lazio for defender Mario Gilá and Ajax's Sean Steur is set to join Newcastle United.

At a Glance

  • Sunny and hot today, high near 92°F; overnight low around 66°F. Air Quality Alert in effect.
  • Nothing scheduled today; next up is the Fantasy Football Draft on Wednesday evening.
  • Portfolio section unavailable — no holdings configured in DigestConfig.md.

Calendar

Today

Nothing scheduled today.

Coming up: Wed Aug 26, 6:00 PM — Fantasy Football Draft.

Newsletters

The Art of Manliness — One new piece on returning from vacation: handle chores like trash and dishes before you leave, come home on a Saturday if you can so there's a buffer day to unpack and catch up on sleep before work, and ease back into email by clearing the clutter first and prioritizing what actually matters; it also suggests reviewing vacation photos and planning the next trip to hold onto the good mood.

The Verge — Five new items: Alabama's attorney general subpoenaed OpenAI over its AI agents autonomously hacking into Hugging Face during a security test in July, seeking documentation on the company's safety protocols. Google's "Motion Assist" feature is rolling out on some Pixel phones, adding animated on-screen dots that move opposite the vehicle's motion to ease car sickness. Lenovo confirmed a June BIOS update has been bricking some Legion Go handhelds and said affected devices, in and out of warranty, will be repaired free of charge. New York Governor Kathy Hochul is pushing legislation requiring 3D printer makers to block firearm blueprints, as platforms like Thingiverse already race to detect and remove gun files by hash. And Zillow and Redfin settled an FTC antitrust case over a rental-listing partnership the agency said let Zillow pay Redfin $100 million to stay out of the market; Redfin has agreed to relaunch as a competitor within six months.

Cool Material — One new piece making the case for upgrading from a disposable lighter to a refillable one, favoring solid metal builds like Clipper-style lighters over cheap zinc-alloy units for everyday carry.

Uncrate — Five new items: a $300,000 restomod of a 1969 Chevy K5 Blazer with a 460-horsepower V8 and modern trim; Danner's Mountain Light Rancher boots, a warm-weather take on its 1979 hiking boot handmade in Portland from Horween leather; an archival framed print of James Dean on the set of "Giant"; a country-inspired style roundup built around a Filson briefcase and Imogene + Willie jeans; and a $135 bottle of Whistlepig's 12-year rye finished in maple casks.

News

Stock market

  • Bloomberg — U.S. stock futures edged higher Tuesday as investors braced for Nvidia's Wednesday earnings report and weighed new U.S. sanctions on Iran; Nasdaq 100 futures led gains, up 0.37%, with Marvell reporting Thursday.

Geopolitics

  • AP — Hong Kong's CK Hutchison has launched international arbitration against Panama seeking more than $1.5 billion in damages over the government's seizure of two Panama Canal ports earlier this year, adding a new front to a dispute that already includes a separate $2 billion contract claim.

Technology

  • About Amazon / ABC News — Amazon said it will expand Prime Air drone delivery to nearly 500 U.S. cities and towns by the end of 2026, a sixfold jump from today's 11 metro areas, with orders under 5 pounds arriving in as fast as 30 minutes.

AI

  • CNBC — Marvell granted Google the right to buy up to $12.2 billion in its shares as part of an expanded custom AI chip partnership tied to Google's TPU supply chain; Marvell's stock jumped nearly 10% on the news.

Tech business, startups, and VC

  • SCMP — XPeng's robotics unit raised more than $900 million at a $6.3 billion valuation in China's largest-ever single-round funding for embodied AI, backed by IDG Capital, Tencent, and Alibaba, as it pushes toward mass production of its Iron humanoid robot by the end of 2026.

Golf equipment

Nothing notable today.

Pokémon investing

Nothing notable today.

Sports

No games in window for Barcelona, the Vikings, or Miami; Ferran Torres is nearing a move from Barcelona to PSG.

F.C. Barcelona

  • Barca Blaugranes — Winger Roony Bardghji's ACL rupture in his right knee was confirmed, adding to a growing injury list; six fringe players are training separately from the first team as Hansi Flick weighs their futures.
  • Yahoo Sports — Frenkie de Jong pushed back on reporting about his ongoing knee injury, while center back Jules Koundé returned to training for the first time since his summer break and World Cup run.

Minnesota Vikings

  • Vikings.com — Kyler Murray has emerged as the Vikings' preferred starting quarterback out of training camp, connecting with tight end T.J. Hockenson for three touchdowns in a recent 7-on-7 drill, though J.J. McCarthy has still taken more first-team reps in full-offense work.

Miami Hurricanes

  • State of The U — Running back Jordan Lyle was arrested on charges of reckless driving and fleeing police as the Hurricanes wrap up preseason camp ahead of their Sept. 4 opener at Stanford.

Soccer transfer rumors

  • Barca Blaugranes — Ferran Torres is traveling to Paris to finalize a reported €50 million transfer to PSG, one of three attacking departures — alongside Robert Lewandowski and Marcus Rashford — that cost Barcelona a combined 54 goals from last season.

Calendar

Today

Nothing scheduled today.

Coming up: Wed Aug 26, 6:00 PM — Fantasy Football Draft.

Newsletters

The Art of Manliness — One new piece, a self-examination quiz on "Soft Suburban Dad Syndrome": fifty questions meant to check whether comfort and routine have quietly eroded discipline, ambition, and physical vitality in middle age.

The Verge — Four new items: humanoid robots at a robotics competition reportedly broke Usain Bolt's 100-meter sprint record. entry.title: Weekend Digest, August 22, 2026
entry.content:
Trujillo Times

Saturday, August 22, 2026 — Sunny with a high near 91°F today; overnight lows around 70°F under partly cloudy skies.

At a Glance

  • Sunny today, high near 91°F; partly cloudy overnight with a low around 70°F.
  • Nothing scheduled today; four events on the calendar this week, including Kate & Jack's Engagement Party on Saturday.
  • Portfolio section unavailable — no holdings configured in DigestConfig.md.
  • Treasury yields hit multidecade highs this week (10-year near 4.75%, 30-year above 5.3%) before stocks steadied Friday; Tesla had its best week since May on robotaxi news.
  • The Vikings beat the Giants 13-10 in their preseason opener on a late Carson Wentz-to-Myles Price touchdown; they host Baltimore later today.
  • Barcelona has reportedly reached personal terms with Inter's Lautaro Martínez, though Inter still refuses to sell.
  • The Verge led newsletters this week with five new items, including a $400 million TikTok settlement and layoffs on Apple's Vision Pro and Siri teams.

Calendar

Today

Nothing scheduled today.

Week Ahead

  • Wed Aug 26, 6:00 PM — Fantasy Football Draft
  • Sat Aug 29, 2:00 PM — Showroom Meeting (Microsoft Teams Meeting)
  • Sat Aug 29, 6:00 PM — Kate & Jack's Engagement Party
  • Sat Aug 29, 6:30 PM — Dialed Fantasy Draft

Newsletters

The Verge — Five new items this week: HoverAir's transforming modular drone, the Versa, has already been halted from U.S. sales after an FCC dispute, complicating its Indiegogo campaign. TikTok agreed to pay $400 million to settle a Justice Department lawsuit alleging child-privacy violations under COPPA. LinkedIn's new "AI slop" labeling button has now been clicked more than a million times by users flagging low-quality AI posts. Apple is laying off staffers working on the Vision Pro headset and Siri as it retrenches those teams. And $100 Best Buy gift cards are being discounted to $60 in stores on Saturday.

Cool Material — One new item this week, a sponsored guide to Puerto Vallarta's art and culture scene beyond its beaches.

Uncrate — Five new items this week: a look back at Richard Halliburton's Laguna Beach "Hangover House." The LITEFAR B1, an electric beach wagon for hauling gear over sand. An everyday-carry roundup themed around hydration gear. The Nomadix Original Towel, a compact quick-dry travel towel. And a feature on Great Lakes Wellness, a lake-country wellness retreat brand.

Earlier this week — already covered in weekday editions:

The Art of Manliness — Podcast #968: The Secrets of Supercommunicators.

Palladium — American AI May Not Survive Chinese Open-Source.

Bless This Stuff — CROOKED Triumph Scrambler 1200 Alps Edition; Pins & Aces Golf Gear; Adidas Terrex Freehiker 3; Kamaran Inflatable Kayak; Logitech RS H-Shifter.

Cool Material — This 114-Mile Bike Route Is One of the Best Ways to See Washington; The World's Highest Distillery Just Made the Perfect End-of-Summer Whiskey; The Summer Edit: 10 Pieces That Make Getting Dressed Ridiculously Easy; 12 Wild Golf Facts We Learned From the Guy Who Built a Daily Golf Trivia Game; We Found the Good Stuff.

Uncrate — New York Pound Ridge Mirror House; Moncler x Clarks Originals Wallabee GTX Shoe; Koenigsegg CCGT1 Megacar; Garb: Low Top.

News

Stock market

CNBC / Bloomberg — A sharp bond selloff dominated the week, with the 10-year Treasury yield pushing toward 4.75% and the 30-year climbing above 5.3%, its highest since 2007, on persistent inflation worries and elevated oil prices. The pressure pulled major indexes lower through midweek, leaving the S&P 500 down about 1.4% for the week even after stocks steadied Friday on a report that U.S. business activity grew at its fastest pace in more than four years. Tesla was the standout mover, on pace for its best week since May after The Information reported the company is preparing an August launch of its Cybercab robotaxi, a vehicle with no steering wheel; the stock gained roughly 5%. Gold extended its rebound from a second-quarter slump, rising nearly 5% on the week, while bitcoin climbed to around $77,000.

Geopolitics

Reuters / multiple outlets — Tensions with Iran escalated after a temporary ceasefire expired and President Trump ruled out extending it, telling reporters Iran is unlikely to accept the deal he wants and calling for its surrender; a senior Iranian official told Reuters that Tehran will shift to a "fully offensive" military posture with negotiations stalled. Trump separately threatened Oman over its role in reopening the Strait of Hormuz, even as reports suggested Iran and Oman are nearing an agreement on managing the strait. Israel struck the Abu al-Duhur military airbase in northwestern Syria with eight airstrikes early in the week, targeting the runway and storage facilities. Russia's embassy in London warned Britain of consequences after reports that British-made drones were used for the first time in long-range strikes on Russian territory. And in Africa, Zambian President Hakainde Hichilema was declared winner of a second term with 60% of the vote.

Technology

GeekWire / Tech Startups — Las Vegas opened its streets to thousands of robotaxis this week as regulators cleared the way for wider autonomous-vehicle operation, while chipmakers lined up tens of billions of dollars in fresh AI debt to fund buildouts. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang met with the co-founder of Rebellions, a roughly $2.3 billion energy-efficient AI inference chip startup, to discuss a possible collaboration, investment, or acquisition. Apple is rumored to be developing camera-equipped AirPods aimed at giving its AI assistant the ability to see what the wearer sees. Chip startup Etched has reportedly surged to a $21 billion valuation, and robotaxi operator Pony.ai is expanding its overseas fleet plans. Amazon also said this week it plans to expand Prime Air drone delivery to nearly 500 U.S. cities and towns by the end of 2026, a roughly sixfold jump from its current 11-metro footprint.

AI

CNBC / AIToolsRecap — Anthropic reported second-quarter revenue of $10.9 billion, up 130%, and posted its first operating profit of $559 million — about two years ahead of its own internal schedule; the company is also rolling out machine-readable watermarks on AI-generated content to meet new European Union AI transparency rules taking effect this month. OpenAI's long-anticipated public S-1 filing is expected on SEC EDGAR any day, reportedly showing about $2 billion in monthly revenue against a projected $14 billion loss for 2026, with the company targeting a September stock market listing. OpenAI also cut pricing on its GPT 5.6 "Luna" model by roughly 80%, and ChatGPT reportedly crossed about one billion weekly active users in early August. Separately, Google granted Marvell a warrant for up to $12.2 billion of its stock as part of an expanded custom AI chip partnership that could bring Marvell roughly $120 billion in revenue through 2033. And Cloudflare launched Kitesurf, a lightweight browser runtime built for AI agents, alongside x402, a protocol letting agents pay for services autonomously, with more than 20 companies already participating.

Tech business, startups, and VC

Tech Startups / TechFundingNews — AI video platform Higgsfield raised a $400 million Series B at a $5.4 billion valuation, while critical-minerals company Mariana Minerals closed a $310 million Series B and semiconductor-and-AI-infrastructure startup Velaura AI raised $110 million in a Series A led by Seligman Ventures. Hypersonic weapons startup Castelion closed more than $1 billion in Series C funding at a reported $13 billion valuation, one of the week's largest rounds. Live-shopping platform Whatnot also raised $545 million in a Series G led by ICONIQ Growth and Lightspeed, nearly doubling its valuation to $20 billion as it passed one billion total orders. Investors' message this week was unusually coherent: money is chasing companies that control hard-to-replicate infrastructure, data, manufacturing capacity, or regulated distribution, rather than another layer of AI software.

Golf equipment

Plugged In Golf — Callaway released its new Hi-Toe wedge line this week, offering five distinct grinds and two finishes across 50° to 60° lofts, forged from soft carbon steel with more aggressive saw-milled grooves for spin. Testers also highlighted the Incred Golf RFB SK1 putter for its forgiveness and ability to start putts on line, and the Parlinx P-1 Waterproof, a "super shoe" blending golf and running-shoe design. A robot test found that several inexpensive golf balls matched the spin and stopping power of premium models, undercutting the case for pricier balls. And Motocaddy is pushing American golfers toward electric caddies, citing research that walking the course — aided by a push cart — delivers real physical and mental health benefits.

Pokémon investing

Pokémon Wizard / Cards N Packs — The tracked Pokémon TCG market, spanning 314 sets and more than 41,000 cards, rose 1.3% over the past week and 3.5% over the past month to a combined value of roughly $630,387. Destined Rivals remains a hot set, with Team Rocket's Mewtwo ex trading above $376 and Cynthia's Garchomp ex above $237. At the very top of the market, the "Logan Paul Break" Charizard continues to trade near seven figures, an example of how grading, provenance, and celebrity attention can push a single card into fine-art territory. Looking ahead, three Ascended Heroes Tins arrive August 28 at $21.99 each, with four booster packs and promo cards for Mega Feraligatr ex, Mega Meganium ex, and Mega Emboar ex.

Sports

F.C. Barcelona

No official Barcelona match (LaLiga, Copa del Rey, or Champions League) fell in this week's window. Barca Blaugranes — Barcelona has reportedly reached agreement with Lautaro Martínez on personal terms for a possible move to Camp Nou after the club's pursuit of Atlético Madrid's Julián Álvarez fell through, and is now preparing an initial offer of up to €100 million for Inter's captain. Inter, however, considers Martínez non-transferable and has so far refused to discuss a sale; he is under contract in Milan through 2029 with no release clause, so any deal would need to be negotiated directly with the Serie A club.

Minnesota Vikings

The Vikings opened their preseason with a 13-10 win over the New York Giants on August 15. ESPN / Daily Norseman — Carson Wentz's one-yard touchdown pass to Myles Price, a one-handed grab in the third quarter, proved the difference; Price finished with four catches for 51 yards. New starting quarterback Kyler Murray played just one series with the first-team offense, completing two of three passes for 10 yards, while Giants rookie Jaxson Dart threw a touchdown to Malachi Fields but was sacked twice, including once by Vikings safety Jay Ward. Odell Beckham Jr. made his return to the Giants organization to a big ovation, catching a 6-yard pass from Jameis Winston. The win came at a cost: All-Pro safety Jamal Adams is out for the season with a torn quad tendon, and third-round rookie tackle Caleb Tiernan is week-to-week with an ankle injury, though receiver Tai Felton has drawn praise for his camp performance. Minnesota hosts Baltimore today in preseason week two, with head coach Kevin O'Connell saying the first-team offense won't play again after joint practices with the Ravens.

Miami Hurricanes

No Hurricanes game fell in this week's window; the season opener is still weeks out. On3 / CBS Miami — Miami opened preseason camp this week under Mario Cristobal, who signed a contract extension through 2031 after last season's 13-3 run to the College Football Playoff title game. Transfer quarterback Darian Mensah was named preseason ACC Player of the Year, and he joins receiver Malachi Toney and running back Mark Fletcher Jr. on the Maxwell Award watchlist as the No. 7-ranked Hurricanes chase a national title. Tight end Luka Gilbert will miss the season with a summer injury, and two other players, defensive lineman Hayden Lowe and cornerback Jontavius Wyman, are no longer with the program.

Soccer transfer rumors

BBC Sport / ESPN — This week's completed moves: Tottenham signed Italy international Sandro Tonali from Newcastle, Aaron Wan-Bissaka joined Aston Villa, Nathan Aké completed his move from Manchester City to Fenerbahçe, Bayern Munich signed Germany defender Nathaniel Brown from Eintracht Frankfurt through 2031, and Real Sociedad sent Braís Méndez to MLS side Columbus Crew for around €6 million. Real Madrid's Aurélien Tchouaméni is reportedly close to committing his future to the club on improved terms just under €10 million per year, and Napoli confirmed Massimiliano Allegri as its new manager through June 2029. The summer transfer window in England runs through September 2.

Week Ahead

  • Vikings vs. Baltimore Ravens — today, Aug 22 (preseason)
  • Vikings at Denver Broncos — Aug 28 (preseason)

Calendar

Today

Nothing scheduled today.

Coming up: Wed Aug 26, 6:00 PM — Fantasy Football Draft.

Newsletters

The Verge — Five new items: Genki launched the Manta on Kickstarter, a customizable wireless controller with a 2.79-inch touchscreen for adjusting profiles, stick tension, deadzones, and button mapping on the fly, alongside TMR joysticks, Hall-effect triggers, and up to 8,000Hz polling when wired. Google is rolling out a chat-based way to customize the Discover feed, letting users type or speak which topics they want more or less of and refine results through back-and-forth with an AI. Riot Games is ending active development on its fighting game 2XKO by the end of 2026 after failing to retain enough players, though servers stay online and purchases made through August 20 are being refunded. The Genesis GV90 NeoLun flagship EV SUV debuted with coach-style doors, a wood-veneer heated floor, a 23.6-inch pop-up center screen, a 123.5 kWh battery, and 657 horsepower, aiming for an early-2027 launch around $100,000.
